review. pi-action itself never forks or rewinds, and no snapshot is ever deleted, so the work it protected stays reachable on the ref. The restore message names the newer snapshot instead.

## Document vs. `Thread-Entry` trailer

A document fits, with one detail. A fork sees a rewindable document *as of the commit that holds its fork entry*. Writing the pointer in a separate commit after the turn would leave a fork at that entry one snapshot
